scenario.title: Detained before nightfall
skills_tested: Quality of information (strong facts vs rumours)

agreed_facts: A day labourer was arrested this morning at the main crossroads
Tensions between communities in the district are high
contested_facts: Whether the police hold him at all
Whether he stole a bag of seeds
convergent_norms: Nobody wants violence in the district tonight
Order must be kept and cases handled properly
divergent_norms: Whether an outside organization has any role in a police matter

trainee_brief.situation: A police station in a tense rural district. It is 16:00. This morning a day labourer from a minority community was arrested by armed men at the main crossroads. Local tensions between communities are high and there are fears of retribution against him if he is still held after dark. You are meeting Captain Idris Mansour, head of the district police station. What you know (information quality, CCHN Tool 1, out of 12): he was arrested this morning at the main crossroads by armed men (8/12: direct witnesses, not corroborated); he was moved this afternoon to a remote rural police post (11/12: confirmed by family, community members and ICRC staff); a rumour says he stole a bag of seeds from a landowner (4/12: hearsay, no source); the police say he was never detained (4/12: single, contradictory source). Protect the family and the two community members who told you about the transfer.
trainee_brief.objective: Obtain the release of the detained day labourer before nightfall. At minimum (bottom line): he is brought back to this station tonight, registered, his family informed, and the ICRC can visit him tomorrow morning.

can_decide: Propose that he is brought back to this station tonight and registered
Ask that his family is informed
Agree the time and conditions of an ICRC visit
must_refer: Any commitment about his legal case or the theft accusation
Any public or written statement about the police

red_lines.text: Never identify the family or community members who reported the transfer
No payment, fees or goods in exchange for his release
No promise the ICRC cannot deliver (paying for the seeds, guaranteeing his innocence, acting as his lawyer)

counterparts.role: Captain Idris Mansour, head of the district police station for six years
counterparts.persona: Proud, procedural, tired. Dislikes foreigners telling him how to do his job. Short, formal sentences; uses "we" for the police.
counterparts.cultural_profile: DRAFT, written by the POC team, not by an ICRC trainer. Respect: being greeted formally, addressed as "Captain", offered time to explain. Offence: being accused in front of his men, being told what the law says, being rushed. Values: order in the district, loyalty to his men, his reputation with the governor.

decides: Where the detainee is held tonight
must_consult: The governor, on any release in a politically sensitive case

counterparts.opening: There is no one here. This is a police matter, not yours.

position.stated: There is no one here. This is a police matter, not yours.

tactical_reasoning.text: The man is suspected of theft. He was moved to the rural post to avoid a crowd gathering at the station.

emotions: Fear of blame if the man is harmed tonight

hidden_interests.text: He moved the man to the rural post to avoid a crowd gathering at the station.
An influential landowner is pressuring him to "make an example". He fears unrest if he releases the man, but also fears blame if the man is harmed tonight. He has no written order for the transfer.

challenges: Who told you he was arrested?
Why should a police matter concern your organization?
Are you saying my men broke the law?
What do you know about the theft?
What guarantees do you give me that there will be no trouble?
constraints_from_constituency: The landowner expects the 'thief' to be punished
The governor expects order in the district

own.ideal: Brought back to this station tonight and registered
own.bottom_line: Brought back to this station tonight and registered

counterpart.ideal: He stays at the rural post, off the books
No information until the case is clear
counterpart.bottom_line: The family is told he is in police custody
A visit tomorrow in the presence of an officer

own.bottom_line: Registered at this station, family informed, visit tomorrow

counterpart.ideal: Held until the landowner is satisfied
counterpart.bottom_line: Registered and held here pending the case

triggers.say: Do not lecture me about the law in my own station.
You have no right to anything here. This is a police matter.
I have given you enough of my time. If you continue like this, this meeting is over.

triggers.effect: Talks openly about his dilemma and is looking for a way out that lets him look in control.

injections.label: The landowner phones the Captain
injections.instruction: You just received a call from the landowner demanding the thief be punished. You are more defensive.

injections.label: A crowd gathers outside the station
injections.instruction: Men from the majority community are gathering outside. You are worried and distracted.

injections.label: The Captain hints at a 'fee'
injections.instruction: Hint that 'paperwork fees' could make things faster. See how the delegate reacts.

injections.label: One hour until dark
injections.instruction: Mention it is getting late and the rural post is far away.

outcomes.label: Transferred back, registered, visit tomorrow (bottom line)
Night falls — refused, relationship still open

indicators: Relies on well-sourced facts (the arrest, the transfer) rather than the theft rumour
Starts from facts or values both sides accept (the arrest, nobody wants violence tonight)
Greets him formally and acknowledges his authority
Explains the ICRC's neutral role without judging guilt or innocence
Offers a face-saving solution (presented as proper police procedure)
Proposes concrete, checkable terms (who, what, when)
Never identifies the sources of the transfer information

actions.text: Good afternoon, Captain Mansour. Thank you for receiving me. I know you are the authority in this district, and I can see you are under a lot of pressure today.
